title: Emergence of Sumerian City-States
description: Independent city-states form in southern Mesopotamia with the first urban centers.

title: Invention of Cuneiform Writing
description: First known writing system emerges from pictographic token accounting in Uruk.

title: Rise of Uruk as Metropolis
description: Uruk grows to ~40,000 people, becoming the largest city in the world.

title: Early Dynastic Period Begins
description: Sumerian city-states enter era of dynastic kingship and frequent warfare.

title: Ziggurat Temple Complexes
description: Massive stepped temples dedicated to city deities become dominant religious architecture.

title: Akkadian Conquest
description: Sargon of Akkad unifies Sumerian city-states under Akkadian rule.

title: Ur III Renaissance
description: Sumerian cultural and political revival under the Third Dynasty of Ur.

title: Sumerian Political Extinction
description: Sumerian identity absorbed into Babylonian culture; language survives only in religious contexts.

title: Sargon Founds Akkadian Empire
description: Sargon of Akkad establishes the world's first empire through conquest.

title: Naram-Sin's Maximum Extent
description: Empire reaches peak territory from the Mediterranean to the Persian Gulf.

title: Gutian Invasion and Collapse
description: Akkadian Empire falls to Gutian invaders combined with internal decay.

title: Unification by Narmer
description: Upper and Lower Egypt unified under the first pharaoh, Narmer.

title: Old Kingdom and Pyramid Age
description: Memphis becomes royal capital; great pyramids of Giza constructed.

title: First Intermediate Period
description: Central authority collapses; regional nomarchs rule independently.

title: Middle Kingdom Reunification
description: Mentuhotep II reunifies Egypt, ushering in Middle Kingdom stability.

title: Bronze Weapons and Chariots
description: New Kingdom military modernizes with horse-drawn chariots and bronze arms.

title: Atenist Monotheism Attempt
description: Akhenaten abolishes traditional polytheism in favor of sun-disk Aten worship.
sources: ["Hornung, Akhenaten and the Religion of Light"]

title: Return to Traditional Religion
description: Tutankhamun restores polytheistic worship; Atenist revolution is erased.
sources: ["Hornung, Akhenaten and the Religion of Light"]

title: Persian Conquest
description: Cambyses II conquers Egypt; becomes a satrapy of the Achaemenid Empire.

title: Hellenization Begins
description: Alexander conquers Egypt; Greek becomes language of administration under Ptolemies.

title: Rise of the Polis
description: Independent city-states (polis) emerge across Greece and Aegean.

title: First Olympic Games
description: Panhellenic religious festivals consolidate Greek cultural identity.

title: Athenian Democracy
description: Cleisthenes establishes the world's first democracy in Athens.

title: Persian Wars Victory
description: Greek city-states repel Persian invasions at Salamis and Plataea.

title: Peloponnesian War
description: Athens and Sparta fight devastating 27-year war ending Athenian hegemony.

title: Alexander's Conquests Begin
description: Alexander the Great begins conquest of Persian Empire and spreads Greek culture.

title: Roman Conquest of Greece
description: Greece becomes a Roman province after sack of Corinth.

title: Roman Republic Founded
description: Overthrow of Tarquin the Proud establishes the Roman Republic.

title: First Punic War
description: Rome challenges Carthage for Mediterranean dominance.

title: Augustus Becomes First Emperor
description: Republic transitions to Empire under Octavian/Augustus.

title: Empire Peaks Under Trajan
description: Maximum territorial extent from Britain to Mesopotamia.

title: Constitutio Antoniniana
description: Caracalla grants Roman citizenship to all free inhabitants of the empire.
sources: ["Garnsey, Aspects of the Decline of the Ancient World"]

title: Edict of Milan
description: Constantine legalizes Christianity, ending official persecution.

title: Capital Moves to Constantinople
description: Constantine founds new eastern capital at Byzantium.

title: Christianity Becomes State Religion
description: Theodosius I makes Nicene Christianity the official state religion.

title: Empire Permanently Divided
description: Death of Theodosius splits Rome into Western and Eastern halves.
sources: ["Heather, The Fall of the Roman Empire"]

title: Fall of the Western Empire
description: Odoacer deposes Romulus Augustulus, ending the Western Roman Empire.
sources: ["Heather, The Fall of the Roman Empire"]

title: Shang Dynasty Founded
description: Tang overthrows Xia; Shang becomes first archaeologically confirmed Chinese dynasty.

title: Oracle Bone Writing
description: Earliest Chinese script emerges on divination bones under King Wu Ding.

title: Bronze Ritual Vessels
description: Shang bronze casting reaches zenith with elaborate ritual vessels.

title: Zhou Conquest at Muye
description: Battle of Muye ends Shang rule; King Wu of Zhou establishes new dynasty.

title: Western Zhou Dynasty Founded
description: Zhou rulers establish Mandate of Heaven doctrine legitimizing rule.

title: Capital Sacked; Eastern Zhou Begins
description: Western Zhou falls to Quanrong; capital moves east to Luoyang.

title: Confucius Born
description: Master Kong's teachings reshape Chinese ethics and social order.

title: Warring States Period Begins
description: Era of intense inter-state warfare and philosophical innovation.

title: Qin Unifies China
description: Qin Shi Huang unifies Chinese states, ending Zhou era.

title: Chandragupta Founds Maurya Empire
description: Chandragupta overthrows Nanda Dynasty, establishes first Indian empire.

title: Ashoka's Conversion to Buddhism
description: Emperor Ashoka embraces Buddhism after Kalinga War; promotes ahimsa.
sources: ["Thapar, Asoka and the Decline of the Mauryas"]

title: Death of Ashoka
description: Empire begins to fragment after Ashoka's death.

title: Shunga Coup Ends Maurya Rule
description: Pushyamitra Shunga assassinates last Maurya emperor.

title: Gupta Dynasty Founded
description: Chandragupta I establishes Gupta Empire in northern India.

title: Golden Age Arts & Sciences
description: Decimal system, zero, astronomy, and classical Sanskrit literature flourish.

title: Hunnic Invasions Collapse Empire
description: Alchon Huns and regional fragmentation end Gupta rule.

title: Cyrus Founds Persian Empire
description: Cyrus the Great overthrows the Medes and founds Achaemenid Empire.

title: Conquest of Babylon
description: Cyrus conquers Babylon; frees Jewish exiles; declares religious tolerance.

title: Darius Reorganizes Empire
description: Darius I establishes satrapy system, royal road, and standardized coinage.

title: Defeat at Marathon
description: Persian invasion of Greece fails at Battle of Marathon.

title: Alexander Conquers Persia
description: Alexander the Great defeats Darius III, ending Achaemenid Empire.

title: Constantinople Founded
description: Constantine establishes new Christian capital at Byzantium.

title: Justinian's Reign Begins
description: Justinian codifies Roman law and reconquers Mediterranean territories.

title: Arab Conquests Begin
description: Byzantines lose Syria, Egypt, and North Africa to the Rashidun Caliphate.
sources: ["Kaegi, Byzantium and the Early Islamic Conquests"]

title: Great Schism
description: Christianity splits into Orthodox and Catholic churches.

title: Fourth Crusade Sacks Constantinople
description: Crusaders sack Constantinople; empire fractures into exile states.

title: Fall of Constantinople
description: Ottomans conquer Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire.

title: Palace Civilization Emerges
description: Great palaces at Knossos, Phaistos, and Malia form cultural centers.

title: Linear A Script
description: Undeciphered Minoan script emerges for administrative use.

title: Thera Volcanic Eruption
description: Catastrophic eruption of Thera devastates Minoan settlements.

title: Mycenaean Takeover
description: Mycenaeans occupy Crete; Linear B replaces Linear A administratively.

title: Shaft Grave Culture Rises
description: Wealthy warrior elites emerge at Mycenae with gold-rich burials.
sources: ["Shelmerdine, Cambridge Companion to the Aegean Bronze Age"]

title: Mycenaeans Expand to Crete
description: Mycenaean Greeks take control of Crete and Aegean trade.
sources: ["Shelmerdine, Cambridge Companion to the Aegean Bronze Age"]

title: Bronze Age Collapse
description: Palace civilization collapses amid widespread Mediterranean upheaval.

title: Mature Harappan Phase
description: Planned cities with grid layouts, drainage, and bath complexes flourish.
sources: ["Kenoyer, Ancient Cities of the Indus Valley"]

title: Climate Shift and Urban Abandonment
description: Climate change and river shifts cause abandonment of major cities.
sources: ["Kenoyer, Ancient Cities of the Indus Valley"]

title: End of Urban Indus Civilization
description: Regional decline complete; populations shift to smaller settlements.
sources: ["Kenoyer, Ancient Cities of the Indus Valley"]

title: Old Kingdom Founded
description: Hattusili I establishes Hittite Old Kingdom with capital at Hattusa.

title: Sack of Babylon
description: Mursili I sacks Babylon, ending First Babylonian Dynasty.

title: Battle of Kadesh
description: Hittites fight Egypt to stalemate; first known peace treaty follows.

title: Bronze Age Collapse
description: Hittite Empire destroyed during broader Sea Peoples upheaval.
